extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and practitioner support staff who file or manage filings via USPTO EFS‑Web / Patent Electronic System
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality requirements for creating, indexing, authenticating, and submitting patent applications and follow-on papers through USPTO EFS‑Web (including practitioner sponsorship, signatures, and image/file formatting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow USPTO PDF Guidelines for EFS-Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must follow the PDF Guidelines for EFS‑Web and PDF Creation for EFS‑Web to ensure that all of the information in the PDF files is successfully received and processed by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the published USPTO PDF creation guidance when generating PDFs for upload so that documents are ingestible and metadata/contents are preserved for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate on-screen data entry
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS‑Web collects information from on-screen entries; the user must provide correct information regarding the type of application, application number, and document type/description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect entries can cause incorrect application file creation, processing delays, filing in the wrong application, or the deciding official not recognizing the submission in time (leading to possible abandonment, withdrawal from issue, or missed publication avoidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select correct application type for new filings
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a new application via EFS‑Web, the user is required to select the correct application type (e.g., design, utility, provisional, nonprovisional) on the EFS‑Web interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system generates application numbers and makes application-type-specific fee codes and document descriptions available. Selecting provisional vs nonprovisional affects fees, processing (e.g., provisionals are not assigned to examiners or published), and further processing—so selection must be correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter correct application/confirmation numbers for follow-on documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting follow-on documents (e.g., replies to Office actions), the user must enter the correct application number, control number or proceeding number, and confirmation number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing an incorrect application/confirmation number pair can result in filing in the wrong application and may cause the intended application to become abandoned for failure to reply. Users cannot file a follow-on document as a new application; check PAIR after submission to confirm correct placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify submission via PAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission, users should log on to PAIR to review the application file and check whether the submitted documents were filed in the correct application and to discover other filing errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking via PAIR helps detect wrong documents, omitted portions, and indexing errors that may require petitions (e.g., petitions under 37 CFR 1.59 or 1.182) to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document indexing and correct document description selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must select from the list of document descriptions to specify the files being submitted (e.g., specification, claims, abstract, drawing; amendment after allowance vs preliminary amendment vs amendment after final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The selected document description assigns a document code used by USPTO systems (IFW, PAIR, SCORE) and routes the submission appropriately. Incorrect indexing may delay processing, route a submission to publication instead of the examiner, or cause other misprocessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund eligibility for fees paid due to system malfunction
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will grant refunds when an EFS‑Web malfunction misled a user into paying a fee in error; refunds are not given where it appears to be user error and no malfunction can be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Patent Electronic Business Center (Patent EBC) for issues. Retain evidence that a system malfunction occurred; without that, refunds are unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication: unique USPTO.gov account and two-step authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: PKI certificates have been discontinued; each registered user must have a unique USPTO.gov account and use the new two-step authentication paradigm for EFS‑Web/PAIR (and the interim Patent Center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts are individual and credentials may only be used by the person to whom they are registered. Sharing of credentials is prohibited. More details at Patent EBC guidance pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship rules and sponsor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may sponsor support staff individuals to access the Patent Electronic System to act under the direction and control of that practitioner; the sponsoring practitioner is responsible for the actions of sponsored individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsored individuals must have their own USPTO.gov accounts, be employees or contractors as described, and sponsorship is limited to those performing support roles. Practitioners must take reasonable steps to verify identity, limit and control access, remove sponsorship when the relationship ends, and ensure compliance with subscriber agreement restrictions (including software use and export rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to file and signature responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered users may access and file follow-on documents in applications in which they are acting on behalf of the applicant; documents submitted through EFS‑Web must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.4, 1.33(b), and 11.18. The person who signs the documents is responsible for the contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsored support staff may file documents properly signed by the practitioner but are not responsible for content if they are not an authorized signer. Joint inventors or partial representatives cannot file documents lacking signatures of all applicants unless specifically authorized. Ink-signed documents can be scanned and e-filed; electronic S-signatures and graphic representations of handwritten signatures are permitted per 37 CFR 1.4(d). Presenting any document constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 11.18(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregistered user filing limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Users without a Patent Electronic System Account may submit new application filings via a non-authenticated workflow as unregistered users, generating a TLS connection for secure transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unregistered users are limited to submission of initial filings (with some exceptions) and may file follow-on documents only by mail (certificate of mailing), Priority Mail Express®, or hand delivery. The USPTO may revoke accounts for improper submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber agreement obligations and account updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Electronic System account holders must update changes in their Verification Form within thirty (30) calendar days and may only use the account for applications authorized to them; unauthorized access may lead to revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscriber agreement also limits sponsorship numbers to a reasonable number the practitioner can control, requires reasonable steps to ensure sponsored users' compliance (including removal when appropriate), and includes restrictions on software use and export controls for application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature formats and recommended identification practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Image attachments' signatures are governed by 37 CFR 1.4(d). Applicants filing via EFS‑Web may use a handwritten signature scanned into a PDF, an S‑signature, or a graphic representation as permitted. A signed transmittal form or application data sheet (ADS) is recommended for identification, and nonpublication requests and accompanying certifications must be signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific subsections of 37 CFR for signature format and be aware that signature and presentation create certifying responsibilities under 37 CFR 11.18(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Grant (eighteen-month) publication request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To request pre-grant publication (voluntary, early, amended, redacted, or republication) via EFS‑Web, users must use the correct form-fillable application data sheet (PTO/AIA/14 or PTO/SB/14) and select the 'Pre-Grant Publication' option on the EFS‑Web data collection screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simply submitting a document requesting publication without selecting the Pre-Grant Publication option is insufficient. To have the publication reflect amended materials, applicant must supply a copy of the application as amended (specification, drawings, ADS/oath/declaration) per 37 CFR 1.215(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination filing steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners submitting requests for supplemental examination via EFS‑Web must select the appropriate filing option (e.g., 'New application/proceeding' then 'Supplemental Examination') or select documents/fees for an existing proceeding and enter the assigned control and confirmation numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the EFS‑Web filing flow for new vs existing supplemental examination matters to ensure proper placement in the supplemental examination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party preissuance and prior-art submissions via EFS‑Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered and unregistered users may submit third‑party preissuance submissions under 37 CFR 1.290 for applicable nonprovisional utility, design, or plant applications by selecting the correct option and entering application and confirmation numbers; submissions are placed in a segregated area for review before possible placement into the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit a 37 CFR 1.501 prior-art/written-statement into a patent file, select 'Prior Art Submission into Patent File under 37 CFR 1.501' and enter Application Number and Patent Number; the patent must be enforceable, and 1.501 submissions cannot be filed via EFS‑Web for design or plant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim copies of foreign priority documents and text-file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim copies of foreign priority documents under 37 CFR 1.55(j) may be submitted via EFS‑Web for specified application types, but a certified copy must be provided before patent grant to perfect the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main parts of the interim copy (Abstract, Drawings, Specification, Claims, Sequence Listing/Computer Program Listings) may be filed as a single PDF and must be indexed using 'Interim copy of Foreign Priority Application'. TXT-only parts (sequence listings, large tables, program listings) may be uploaded as TXT files (or on compact disc) with specific file-naming conventions (start with country code and foreign application number, indicate part order if split), and sequence listings over 25 MB must be split into multiple files under the 25 MB upload limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and drawings: permitted types and quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white line drawings are required per 37 CFR 1.84(a)(1), with exceptions permitting color drawings in design applications and certain situations where photographs or color drawings are the only practicable medium. Photographs and color drawings must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in black and white for publication and printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings are not ordinarily permitted in utility applications without a petition under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2). Color or grayscale images filed in utility applications as 'drawings - other than black and white line drawings' will be converted to black and white and may degrade. For international (PCT) filings, PCT Rule 11.13 prohibits color drawings and usually prohibits photographs; black & white photographs accepted only where impossible to present as drawings. Conversion to B/W by RO/US or the International Bureau may lose detail, potentially affecting disclosure. Objections and requests for correction/deletion may follow noncompliant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which application types may include non-BW drawings/photos
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, color drawings, grayscale drawings, and other non-black-and-white line drawings may be submitted via EFS‑Web only in specified application types and proceedings (listed: nonprovisional design applications, provisional applications, nonprovisional utility applications, U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, international design applications, reexamination proceedings, supplemental examination proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only black and white photographs and black & white line drawings may be submitted in international (PCT) applications. Select the correct document description to match the filing type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document description choices for drawings/photographs (DRW vs DRW.NONBW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must select the correct document description: 'Drawings – only black and white line drawings' (DRW) for true B/W line drawings, or 'Drawings – other than black and white line drawings' (DRW.NONBW) for photographs, color drawings, grayscale drawings, and other non-B/W drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DRW files will be converted into TIFF and stored in IFW (or SCORE + IFW placeholder for design). DRW.NONBW files are stored in SCORE, with a black and white copy stored in IFW and a SCORE placeholder. Incorrect selection may cause processing in a quality insufficient for examination/publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image scanning resolution and orientation recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure reproducibility in black and white for eighteen-month publication and printed patents, images should be scanned at a minimum resolution of 300 DPI; for international design applications, resolution should be between 250x250 DPI and 300x300 DPI, with a 1–20 pixel border and at least a one-pixel border.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFS‑Web supports color/grayscale but converts many images to black and white when stored; scanning at recommended resolutions and avoiding landscape orientation (PAIR displays portrait only) reduces the risk of degraded images or distortion. Landscape drawings may be auto-converted to portrait and become distorted.
